chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When you pray while facing away from the Qiblah, and it becomes clear to you that you prayed facing away from the Qiblah while you were within the time [of that prayer], then repeat [the prayer]; and if the time has passed you, then do not repeat."

key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: The Qiblah (direction of prayer towards the Kaaba)
key_terms.فَأَعِدْ: Then repeat (imperative to perform the prayer again)

ai.seo_question: Do I need to repeat my prayer if I realize I was facing the wrong direction after the prayer time has ended?
ai.summary: This ruling from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between *qada* (making up) and *ada* (performing on time) based on the timing of the error. It reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that the validity of the initial prayer is not voided by the Qiblah misalignment, but the obligation to repeat it depends on whether the prayer's specific time window remains open. This principle underscores the practical ease (*taysir*) in Shia fiqh, prioritizing the completion of the obligatory act over strict ritual perfection if the time constraint prevents correction.
